plan: In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding one's true value is the dominant strategy since the payment depends on the second-highest bid, not your own bid. Overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth if I win but others bid high; underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. With a value of $13, I should bid exactly $13 to maximize expected profit regardless of competitors' strategies.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction. In such auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy: if I win, I pay the second-highest bid regardless of my own bid, and if I bid higher than my value, I risk winning and paying more than the item is worth; if I bid lower, I risk losing an item that would have been profitable. Since my value is $49 (the maximum possible), bidding my true value maximizes expected profit without unnecessary risk.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding one's true value is a dominant strategy: it maximizes expected profit regardless of others' bids, since you only pay the second-highest bid if you win, and bidding truthfully ensures you win whenever it's profitable to do so. With my value at $44, I will bid exactly $44 to guarantee I never overpay or miss profitable wins.
